finding.claim: The iconUrl parameter of PUT /profile is stored with no validation. The nightly sync job later issues a server-side GET to it, so an attacker can make the server request internal hosts, cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), localhost services, or any other URL. The response bytes are fetched into memory. The webhookUrl field is not vulnerable because it is fully validated.
finding.source: `icon` argument of Profile.update(), the body of PUT /profile (line 11)

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives attacker-controlled icon from PUT /profile
this.iconUrl = icon stored with no scheme, host or IP validation
sync() (nightly job) calls URI.create(iconUrl) and sends a GET with the server's HttpClient

finding.guards_checked: Only the webhook argument is validated (line 12, String.matches does a full match against https://hooks.example.com/[A-Za-z0-9]{20}). The icon argument has no check on the path. No allowlist, scheme check or private-IP block was found anywhere else in the codebase, which is a single file. The webhookUrl sink at line 21 is not reported because the full-match regex pins the scheme, host and path.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the unvalidated `icon` argument, and src/Profile.java:23 sends a GET to URI.create(iconUrl). Only `webhook` is checked, by the full-match regex at line 12.
